questions.question: What do you call the drugs that bind to the receptor site and inhibit its natural function?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Antagonist** is a chemical substance that binds to and block the activation of certain receptors on cells, preventing a biological response.
 
• **Example: Naloxone is a competitive antagonist for the opioid receptor**
 
• These are the substances that reduce **arousal and stimulation.**

 
• They affect the** central nervous system**, slowing down the messages b/w the brain and body.
 
• They can affect concentration and coordination b/w and slow down the activity of a person to some extent.
 
• **As the name indicates these are the drugs used to depress the actions.​**

• **Antidepressants: **

 
 
• These are the drugs used to treat or prevent clinical depression.
 
• They can also be used to treat some other conditions, including. 
 
• Observing compulsive disorder.
 
• generalized anxiety disorder.
 
• Post-traumatic stress disorder
 
• Sometimes it is used to treat people with long-term chronic pain.
 
 
 
• **Agonist: **
 
 
• It is a drug or chemical substance that binds with a receptor and activates it to induce the action or response.
 
• These have an intrinsic efficacy and affinity for the receptor that results in binding to it.
 
• This binding results in changes in the receptors' functioning in the host cells.

questions.question: In which of the following cases the Supreme Court, while laying out the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution held that the democratic character of the polity was an essential component of the ‘basic structure’?

options.text: Sajjan Singh vs State of Rajasthan
Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala
Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras
A K Gopalan vs State of Madras

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The case of Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala** in **1973** was a landmark decision that introduced the Basic Structure Doctrine into **Indian constitutional law**.
 
• This doctrine asserts that democracy founded on free and fair elections is a fundamental feature of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It serves as a safeguard, protecting the essential elements of the democratic system from arbitrary alterations or infringements.
 
• According to the** Basic Structure Doctrine, **any constitutional amendment that seeks to modify the basic structure of the Constitution is deemed invalid.
 
• This principle aims to uphold the integrity of Indian democracy and safeguard the rights and liberties of its citizens.
 
• **Justice Hans Raj Khanna **asserted that the constitution possesses a basic structure of constitutional principles and values.
 
• The 13-judge Constitution bench of the Supreme Court deliberated on the limitations, if any, of the powers of the elected representatives of the people and the nature of the fundamental rights of an individual.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 1965 case Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan** established the foundational principles of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **In the Romesh Thapar Case Verdict, **the Court determined that freedom of speech and expression encompasses the freedom to circulate ideas, ensuring their dissemination.
 
• **A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras**, AIR 1950 SC 27, was a significant ruling by the Supreme Court of India, where it clarified that Article 21 of the Constitution did not necessitate Indian courts to apply a due process of law standard.

questions.question: Which winds blow across the Asian continent at latitudes north of the Himalayas roughly parallel to the Tibetan highlands?

__
 
• **Jet streams** are **high-altitude winds** that traverse the **Asian continent **above the latitudes north of the Himalayas, running roughly parallel to the **Tibetan highlands**.
 
• The Tibetan highlands act as a dividing line, splitting the jet streams into north and south branches, with the northern branch significantly influencing **winter weather patterns** in India.
 
• These fast-flowing air currents are typically observed at altitudes of up to 3 km in the lower troposphere.
 
• Furthermore, at higher elevations, between 9 to 13 km above the Earth's surface, westerly winds persistently blow across Western and Central Asia from west to east.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The trade winds** are consistent winds that blow from east to west, occurring just north and south of the equator.
 
• **Southwest winds** carry warm air from the tropics and gradually cool as they travel northward over the sea.
 
• Northwest winds originate from the northwest direction and blow in a southeastward direction.

questions.question: In which year did Albert Einstein predict a new state of matter, the Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), based on a quantum formulation by the Indian physicist Satyendra Nath Bose?

• **Albert Einstein's **prediction of the **Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) in 1924** was based on the quantum formulations put forth by Indian physicist **Satyendra Nath Bose**.
 
• This groundbreaking state of matter, often referred to as the** fifth state of matter,** was a result of Bose's foundational work on quantum mechanics in the early 1920s.
 
• Bose's contributions included the development of Bose-Einstein statistics and the theoretical framework for the BEC.
 
• The first** "pure" **BEC was subsequently created by Eric Cornell, Carl Wieman, and their colleagues at JILA on June 5, 1995.
 
• In a notable advancement, the **Cold Atom Laboratory experiment **conducted aboard the International Space Station achieved the creation of a BEC consisting of rubidium atoms in June 2020.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satyendra Nath Bose, **an Indian mathematician and physicist, was highly regarded for his contributions to theoretical physics, particularly in the field of quantum mechanics during the early 1920s.
 
• His notable achievements include laying the groundwork for Bose-Einstein statistics and formulating the theory of the Bose-Einstein condensate.
 
• Recognized for his scholarly pursuits, Bose was elected as a Fellow of the Royal Society.
 
• In acknowledgment of his outstanding contributions to science, the Government of India conferred upon him the Padma Vibhushan, the nation's second highest civilian award, in 1954.

questions.question: Who among the following designed a campaign that came to be known as the ‘Rowlatt Satyagraha’?

• **Mahatma Gandhi** spearheaded the **Rowlatt Satyagraha campaign**, a **pivotal chapter** in India's struggle for independence.
 
• This **non-violent civil disobedience movement** unfolded in** 1919 **as a response to the Rowlatt Act, an oppressive law enacted by the** British colonial government.**
 
• The act granted authorities the authority to detain individuals without trial for up to two years, a measure deemed unjust and repressive by Gandhi and his supporters.
 
• Gandhi, recognizing the urgency of opposing this** draconian legislation**, called for a nationwide hartal, or strike, to denounce the Rowlatt Act.
 
• The response was resounding, with the hartal gaining widespread support and catalyzing a wave of demonstrations and protests throughout India.

• **The Rowlatt Satyagraha** served as a potent catalyst in raising awareness about the injustices perpetuated by British rule.
 
• It underscored the efficacy of non-violent resistance as a formidable tool in the fight for freedom and equality.
 
• Moreover, the movement marked a personal triumph for Gandhi, showcasing his leadership prowess and charismatic influence over the Indian populace.
 
• The Rowlatt Satyagraha stands as a testament to the indomitable spirit of the Indian people and their unwavering commitment to securing their rights and liberties through peaceful means.

questions.question: What was the target growth rate of the Indian economy in the second five-year plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__4.5%__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The second five-year plan, **spanning from **1956 to 1961, **aimed for a **target growth rate **of** 4.5% **for the Indian economy.
 
• However, the actual growth rate fell slightly short at **4.27%**.
 
• **Drafted by P.C. Mahalanobis**, this plan prioritized rapid industrialization and the development of the public sector, with an emphasis on achieving quick structural transformation.
 
• To protect domestic industries, the government implemented tariffs on imports, while also allocating nearly 50 billion rupees across various sectors to meet set targets.
 
• Additionally, the plan advocated for the adoption of new technology and efficient investments to propel India's annual national income growth.
 
• Despite its objectives, the second five-year plan faced criticism from classical liberal economist **B.R. Shenoy**.
 
• He argued that the plan's heavy reliance on deficit financing to promote industrialization posed significant risks and could potentially lead to economic instability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan** placed a significant emphasis on the development of the public sector and aimed for **"rapid industrialization."**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true for Indian monsoons?

options.text: Monsoonal rainfall is affected by jet streams
Monsoonal rainfall is the lifeline of Indian agriculture
Himalayas play an important role in monsoonal rainfall
Monsoonal rainfall is not affected by the relief features of the country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monsoonal rainfall is not affected by the relief features of the country**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Monsoonal rainfall is not affected by the relief features of the country **is** NOT true for Indian monsoons.**
 
• Monsoonal rainfall in India is indeed influenced by various geographical and atmospheric factors, including relief features such as mountains and plateaus.
 
• **For example, **mountains like the **Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats** influence rainfall distribution through orographic lifting, while coastal areas often experience different rainfall patterns due to their proximity to the sea. Overall, relief features play a crucial role in shaping the spatial distribution of monsoonal rainfall across India.
 
• Therefore, statement 4, which suggests that monsoonal rainfall is not affected by relief features, is not accurate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monsoonal rainfall is affected by jet streams: **This statement is true. Jet streams, particularly the subtropical westerly jet stream, play a significant role in the onset, intensity, and distribution of monsoonal rainfall in India. Changes in the position and strength of jet streams can influence the behavior of monsoon systems.
 
• **Monsoonal rainfall is the lifeline of Indian agriculture:** This statement is true. Monsoonal rainfall is crucial for agriculture in India, as it provides the majority of the water needed for crop cultivation. The timely arrival and distribution of monsoon rains are essential for crop growth and overall agricultural productivity.
 
• **Himalayas play an important role in monsoonal rainfall:** This statement is true. The Himalayan mountain range acts as a barrier to the moisture-laden monsoon winds coming from the Indian Ocean. As these winds encounter the Himalayas, they are forced to rise, leading to orographic rainfall on the windward side of the mountains. This process significantly contributes to the overall monsoonal rainfall pattern in India.

questions.question: The main function of centriole is:

__
 
• **Centrioles** are paired** barrel-shaped organelles f**ound in the **cytoplasm of animal cells**, typically situated near the **nuclear envelope**.
 
• They play a crucial role in organizing **microtubules**, which act as the cell's structural framework.
 
• Additionally, centrioles aid in determining the positioning of the nucleus and other organelles within the cell.
 
• Each centriole resides within the centrosome, an area of the cytoplasm located adjacent to the nucleus.
 
• The centrosome, considered an organelle, contains two centrioles.
 
• Composed of microtubules, centrioles are integral to cell division processes and are essential for maintaining cellular structure and function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Centrioles **consist of **nine groups of microtubule triplets** arranged in a cylindrical configuration, a detailed structure that can only be observed under an electron microscope.
 
• These microtubule triplets are interconnected and oriented at right angles to each other, contributing to the centriole's overall stability and function.
 
• However, there are exceptions to this typical centriolar organization. For instance, in the embryos of Drosophila melanogaster, nine pairs of microtubules are formed instead of the usual microtubule triplets.
 
• Similarly, premature embryos and sperm cells of Caenorhabditis elegans exhibit a unique arrangement of nine single microtubules, deviating from the standard centriolar structure observed in most animal cells.

questions.question: Recoveries of loans and advances, borrowings, are an example of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**capital receipts**__.

__
 
• **Recoveries of loans and advances**, borrowings, are an example of **capital receipts**.
 
• **Capital receipts **encompass funds received by the government that either **create liabilities or reduce financial** assets.
 
• They represent incoming cash flows and can be categorized as both non-debt and debt receipts.
 
• Examples of capital receipts include loans obtained from the general public, foreign governments, and the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
• Additionally, borrowings from foreign countries and institutions, as well as borrowings from the RBI, are considered capital receipts.
 
• The recovery of loans extended by the central government to states and other entities also falls under this category.
 
• On the balance sheet, capital receipts are typically listed in the liabilities section. It's important to note that capital receipts generally do not recur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Non-tax revenue **constitutes income generated by the government from sources other than taxes. These receipts include earnings from various sources such as interest on loans, dividends on investments (e.g., from Public Sector Undertakings), fees, and revenues from services provided by the government.
 
• **Revenue receipts** represent the income derived by a business from its routine operational activities. These receipts are recurring and directly impact the profit and loss statement of the business.
 
• **Tax revenue, **on the other hand, refers to the total receipts generated by the government from taxes and other duties.

questions.question: In 1957, who redefined a model that predicted the shape of individual molecules based on the extent of electron-pair electrostatic repulsion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nyholm and Gillespie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ronald Gillespie and Ronald Nyholm **significantly enhanced the **valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) model** in **1957,** refining its level of detail and its ability to discern between various molecular geometries.
 
• The **VSEPR theory** represents a **foundational concept in chemistry,** offering a straightforward explanation for the shapes of molecules.
 
• It posits a direct relationship between molecular geometry and the count of valence electrons, further providing predictions for precise molecular structures, including bond angles.
 
• The theory was initially proposed by **Nevil Sidgwick and Herbert Powell** in 1940, yet its roots trace back to Ryutaro Tsuchida of Japan, who originally suggested the notion of a correlation between molecular geometry and the number of valence electron pairs in 1939.
 
• However, it was the contributions of Gillespie and Nyholm that significantly expanded and refined the VSEPR model, solidifying its position as a fundamental tool in the study of molecular structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The VSEPR model**, or the Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion model, offers predictions for** the geometry of the majority of polyatomic molecules and ions.**
 
• It achieves this by solely considering the count of electron pairs surrounding the central atom, while disregarding all other valence electrons.
 
• According to the model, **lone pairs of electrons localize** on the central atom, while each bonded pair is shared between two atoms.
 
• The lone pair electrons in a molecule occupy a larger spatial region compared to the bonding pairs of electrons.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Vice President of the Interim Government formed by Congress in 1946?

• Jawaharlal Nehru, as the Vice President of the Council, wielded powers akin to those of a Prime Minister.

• Following independence, all members of this council would be Indians, except for the Viceroy, who in August transitioned to the role of Governor-General.

questions.question: What do you call the fluid matrix filling in the cell?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytoplasm** is a** gelatinous fluid **occupying the **space within a cell,** which serves as the region between the **plasma membrane and the nucleus**.
 
• It encompasses both the** cytosol,** a semi-fluid portion, and various organelles suspended within it.
 
• Notably,** prokaryotic cells **lack membrane-bound organelles characteristic of eukaryotic cells, such as mitochondria or endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• Instead, their cytoplasm contains various structures essential for cellular functions, albeit without the distinct membrane boundaries seen in eukaryotic organelles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ribosomes** are large ribonucleoprotein complexes found ubiquitously in all cells. Comprising both RNA and proteins, ribosomes play a crucial role in translating genetic information stored in mRNA into polypeptide chains.
 
• **Plasmids** are small, extrachromosomal DNA molecules present within a cell, physically distinct from the chromosomal DNA and capable of replicating independently. They often carry non-essential genes that may confer advantages such as antibiotic resistance.
 
• Discovered in 1897 by Italian physician Camillo Golgi, the Golgi complex is a cellular organelle consisting of five to eight flattened membrane-bound sacs known as cisternae. It plays a vital role in processing, modifying, and packaging proteins and lipids for transport within the cell or secretion outside the cell.

questions.question: E, F, G, and H are four points lying on the circumference of a circle to make a cyclic quadrilateral. If ∠FGH = 57°, then what will be the measure of the ∠HEF?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

E, F, G, and H are four points lying on the circumference of a circle to make a cyclic quadrilateral.

∠FGH = 57°

**Concept Used:**

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the opposite angles are supplementary. This means that the sum of the measures of each pair of opposite angles is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d8fe5e7cc851df6501e59d916fc12238a073d8044a75dd67efc5779db4b568e.png]

Substituting the given value of ∠FGH:

Solving for ∠HEF:

__Shortcut Trick__

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2.

Similarly, x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (k² − 2)² − 2.

Here, a + 1/a = 3, so k = 3.

a⁴ + 1/a⁴ = 7² − 2 = 49 − 2 = 47.

**∴ The correct answer is 47.**

a + 1/a = 3

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

⇒ (a + 1/a)² = 3²

⇒ a² + 1/a² + 2(a)(1/a) = 9

⇒ a² + 1/a² + 2 = 9

⇒ a² + 1/a² = 9 − 2

⇒ a² + 1/a² = 7

⇒ Squaring both sides again:

⇒ (a² + 1/a²)² = 7²

⇒ a⁴ + 1/a⁴ + 2(a²)(1/a²) = 49

⇒ a⁴ + 1/a⁴ + 2 = 49

⇒ a⁴ + 1/a⁴ = 49 − 2

⇒ a⁴ + 1/a⁴ = 47

**∴ The correct answer is 47.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

We’ve sent a very strong protest letter. That should make them sit up and __take notice__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4 i.e. Consider.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase** "sit up and take notice" **means to pay careful attention to something or someone because they are interesting or important. 

 
 
• **Example:** When the new CEO implemented the innovative policy, it made the whole industry sit up and take notice.
 
 
 
• The word **"Consider" **means to think carefully about something, typically before making a decision. 
 
 
• **Example**: Before buying the house, they considered all its pros and cons.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Consider.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Follow** means to go or come after a person or thing proceeding ahead. 

 
 
• **Example**: She followed the instructions carefully to assemble the furniture.
 
 
 
• **Attend** means to be present at an event, meeting, or function.
 
 
• **Example**: He attended the conference to gain insights into the latest industry trends.
 
 
 
• **Observe** means to notice or perceive (something) and register it as being significant. 
 
 
• **Example**: The scientist observed the reactions under the microscope carefully.
